items.prompt: assertTransition is called with the action name 'cancel', which has no row in the TRANSITIONS table. What does it do?
items.answer: Throws a 409 conflict with Unknown sprint action "cancel"
distractors: Returns the current state unchanged, so the write changes nothing
Throws a plain Error naming "cancel", which is reported as a 500
Returns null, and the service then skips its sprint update
items.explanation: const t = TRANSITIONS[action]; if (!t) throw conflict(`Unknown sprint action "${action}"`). conflict() builds an ApiError with code CONFLICT, which maps to status 409.

items.prompt: Sprint S held issues of 5 and 3 points. It was completed with moveUnfinishedTo 'backlog' while only the 5-point issue sat in a DONE column. What does sprintReport show for S now?
items.answer: committed 5, completed 5, total 1, with unfinished empty
distractors: committed 8, completed 5, total 2, with the 3-point issue unfinished
committed 8, completed 8, total 2, since completion closes all work
committed 0, completed 0, total 0, as a completed sprint is empty
items.explanation: Completion set the 3-point issue's sprintId to null. sprintReport reads the issues whose sprintId is still S, so only the DONE 5-point issue is counted: committed 5, completed 5, total 1, unfinished [].

items.prompt: An ACTIVE sprint holds three issues: 5 points in a DONE column, 3 points in progress, and one in progress with storyPoints null. What does sprintReport return?
items.answer: committed 8, completed 5, total 3, and two unfinished issues
distractors: committed 8, completed 5, total 2, as unestimated issues are skipped
committed 8, completed 5, total 3, and just one unfinished issue
It throws a 409, because one issue in the sprint has no estimate
items.explanation: Both sums use (i.storyPoints ?? 0), so the null issue adds 0 to committed (8) and is still in total (3). unfinished is every issue not in a DONE column: the 3-point one and the null one.

items.prompt: completeSprint is called on an ACTIVE sprint with moveUnfinishedTo set to the string 'backlog'. What happens to its unfinished issues?
items.answer: Their sprintId becomes null, as 'backlog' is mapped to null first
distractors: A 404 Destination sprint, since no sprint row has the id 'backlog'
Their sprintId is set to the literal string 'backlog' by the update
A 409, because 'backlog' is not a PLANNED sprint of this project
items.explanation: Line 79 maps 'backlog' to null before the transaction, so the destination checks (if (destination)) are skipped and the bulk update writes sprintId: null.

items.prompt: Issue GJ-7 still sits in a COMPLETED sprint. A member sends a sprint assignment with sprintId null and a current expectedUpdatedAt. What does assignIssueToSprint do?
items.answer: Moves it to the backlog, since the sprint checks need a sprintId
distractors: Refuses with 409, as a completed sprint keeps its issues locked
Refuses with 404, because a null sprintId finds zero sprint rows
Moves it, but leaves updatedAt alone because the sprint field was null
items.explanation: The sprint lookup and the COMPLETED check sit inside if (sprintId), so null skips them. The updateMany then writes sprintId: null and a new updatedAt.

items.prompt: A user who is a VIEWER of project GJ sends a sprint assignment for one of its issues. What comes back?
items.answer: 403: Your role (VIEWER) is not permitted to sprint:manage
distractors: 404: the project is hidden, as viewers count as outsiders here
200: a viewer may read sprints, and so may assign to them
409: a viewer's expectedUpdatedAt is treated as a stale token
items.explanation: assignIssueToSprint loads the project with 'sprint:manage'. The viewer is a member, so requireMembership passes, but the policy lists only ADMIN and MEMBER for sprint:manage and authorize throws forbidden (403).

items.prompt: Another sprint of the project is already ACTIVE. Someone starts a PLANNED sprint of it that has no issues. Which error does startSprint return?
items.answer: 409 "Cannot start a sprint with no issues" from the state machine
distractors: 409 "Another sprint is already active in this project" from P2002
404 Sprint, since an empty sprint is filtered out of the lookup
None: it starts, as the issue count is only checked at completion
items.explanation: assertTransition('start', ...) runs its guard with issueCount 0 before any update, so the no-issues conflict is thrown first and the unique index is never reached.

items.prompt: completeSprint is called on ACTIVE sprint S with moveUnfinishedTo set to the id of S itself. What is the outcome?
items.answer: 409 "Unfinished issues cannot stay in the completed sprint"
distractors: 409 "Unfinished issues can only move to a planned sprint"
200: the unfinished issues simply stay attached to S
404 Destination sprint, as S is excluded from that lookup
items.explanation: The destination === sprint.id check comes first inside if (destination), so it throws before the destination lookup and the PLANNED check run.

items.prompt: Issue GJ-3 is already in PLANNED sprint P. A member assigns it to P again with a current expectedUpdatedAt. What does assignIssueToSprint return?
items.answer: The issue, with its updatedAt moved forward by the write
distractors: The issue unchanged, as nothing about it is different
A 409, as the issue is already assigned to that same sprint
A 204 with an empty body, since a repeated assignment is skipped
items.explanation: Nothing compares the old and new sprintId. The sprint exists and is not COMPLETED, the token matches, so updateMany writes the same sprintId with a new updatedAt and the issue is returned (200).

items.prompt: A member creates a sprint with only a name and goal, then immediately calls completeSprint on it. What comes back?
items.answer: 409 "Cannot complete a sprint that is PLANNED (must be ACTIVE)"
distractors: 409 "Sprint was already completed" from the guarded updateMany
200 with movedCount 0, since the new sprint has no issues to move
404 Sprint, because a sprint cannot be found until it is started
items.explanation: A new sprint gets state PLANNED from the schema default. completeSprint calls assertTransition('complete', 'PLANNED') at line 85, which throws before the updateMany guard runs.

items.prompt: Issue GJ-9 is assigned to user U. A member PATCHes it with { assigneeId: null } and nothing else. What does updateIssue do?
items.answer: Clears the assignee and logs assignee.changed, with no notification
distractors: Leaves U assigned, because null is treated like a field left out
Clears the assignee and enqueues issue.assigned for the old user U
Clears the assignee but writes no activity, as no one was assigned
items.explanation: 'assigneeId' in patch copies null into data, so the update clears it and the activity entry is recorded (null differs from U). The notification needs a truthy data.assigneeId, so none is enqueued.

items.prompt: A project VIEWER requests the report of one of the project's sprints. What does sprintReport do?
items.answer: Returns the report, because its default action sprint:read admits VIEWER
distractors: Refuses with 403, since the report needs sprint:manage like writes
Refuses with 404 for the project, as viewers are not shown sprints
Returns the report, but with the story point sums hidden from the viewer
items.explanation: sprintReport calls loadProject without an action, so the default 'sprint:read' applies, and the policy grants sprint:read to ADMIN, MEMBER and VIEWER.

items.front: The three separate protections inside assignIssueToSprint
items.back: Isolation: the serializable( call (line 137). Ownership/lifecycle guards: the project-scoped sprint lookup and the COMPLETED rejection (lines 143-150). Optimistic version check: the updatedAt term in the updateMany predicate (line 156) plus changed.count === 0 -> 409 (lines 160-162). Each has its own failing test.

items.front: Four gaps in the pre-change completeSprint
items.back: (a) sprint state and unfinished count were read outside the transaction; (b) sprint.update had no state: ACTIVE guard, so two completions could both succeed; (c) moveUnfinishedTo was never checked, so a foreign or completed sprint id was accepted; (d) movedCount came from a count() before the move.

items.front: Why does the sprint suite opt out of the rollback proxy?
items.back: Competing operations need separate, real PostgreSQL transactions to exercise isolation and constraints; a rollback wrapper would put them in one. sprint.test.js:8 sets globalThis.__NO_ROLLBACK__ = true and setup.js:39 honors it.

items.front: Why does the nonmember test read the issue through __realClient instead of the API?
items.back: The outsider's API reads would also return 404. Reading the row directly is the only way to show that neither sprintId nor updatedAt changed after the denied write.
